questions.prompt: The number \(\sqrt{5}\) belongs to the set of ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 1. \(\sqrt{5}\) cannot be written as a fraction of integers, so it is irrational.

questions.prompt: Which of the following intervals represents the set \(\{x \mid -1<x\le 3\}\)?
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 2. \(-1\) is excluded (open) and \(3\) is included (closed).

questions.prompt: The solution set of the inequality \(3x-1\le 2x+3\) is ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 3. \(3x-2x\le 3+1\Rightarrow x\le 4\).

questions.prompt: The solution set of the inequality \(|2x+1|<1\) is ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 4. \(-1<2x+1<1\Rightarrow -2<2x<0\Rightarrow -1<x<0\).

questions.prompt: The solution set of the inequality \(x^2+x-2<0\) is ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 5. \(x^2+x-2=(x+2)(x-1)\) is negative between its roots \(-2\) and \(1\).
Midterm 2024, question 6. \(f(3)=\frac{\sqrt{4}}{9}=\frac{2}{9}\).

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a polynomial?
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 7. \(\frac{1}{x}=x^{-1}\) has a negative power, so \(h\) is not a polynomial; the constants \(\sqrt5\) and \(\frac12\) are allowed.

questions.prompt: The function \(f(x)=\sqrt[5]{3x+4}\) is a ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 8. It is a root of an expression in \(x\): a radical function.

questions.prompt: The domain of the function \(f(x)=-2x^3+4x^2+x-1\) is ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 9. A polynomial is defined for every real number.

questions.prompt: Consider the functions \(f(x)=4x+1\) and \(g(x)=x^2-1\). Then the domain of \(\frac{f}{g}\) is ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 10. \(\frac{f}{g}\) needs \(g(x)=x^2-1\ne 0\), so \(x\ne\pm1\).

questions.prompt: The domain of the function \(f(x)=\sqrt{2x-4}\) is ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 11. \(2x-4\ge 0\Rightarrow x\ge 2\).

questions.prompt: The range of the function shown in the graph is ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 12. The graph goes from height 5 down to 0 at the origin and back up to 5: the \(y\)-values fill \([0,5]\).

image.alt: V-shaped graph: line segments from (-5, 5) down to (0, 0) and up to (5, 5).

questions.prompt: Are the functions \(f(x)=\frac{x^2-9}{x-3}\) and \(g(x)=x+3\) the same?
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 13. \(D_f=\mathbb{R}-\{3\}\) but \(D_g=\mathbb{R}\); equal functions need the same domain.

questions.prompt: The \(x\)-intercepts of the graph of the function \(y=x^2-4\) are ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 14. \(x^2-4=0\Rightarrow x=\pm2\).

questions.prompt: The \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the function \(y=x^2-4\) is ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 15. At \(x=0\), \(y=-4\).

questions.prompt: A function \(f\) is even if its graph is symmetric with respect to ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 16. Even: \(f(-x)=f(x)\), so the graph is symmetric about the \(y\)-axis.

questions.prompt: The function \(f(x)=\frac{x-2x^3}{x^2+1}\) is ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 17. \(f(-x)=\frac{-x+2x^3}{x^2+1}=-f(x)\).

questions.prompt: If \(f(x)=\frac{1}{x+1}\) and \(g(x)=\sqrt{x+3}\), then \((f\circ g)(x)=\) ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 18. \((f\circ g)(x)=f(\sqrt{x+3})=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x+3}+1}\).

questions.prompt: If \(f(x)=\frac{1}{x+1}\) and \(g(x)=\sqrt{x+3}\), then the domain of \(f\circ g\) is ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 19. Need \(x+3\ge0\); and \(\sqrt{x+3}+1\ge1\) is never 0. So \(x\ge -3\).

questions.prompt: The relation \(f(x)=5x-3\) is ...
options: a function that is not one-to-one
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 20. \(5x_1-3=5x_2-3\Rightarrow x_1=x_2\).

questions.prompt: The relation \(f(x)=x^2-1\) is ...
options: a function that is not one-to-one
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 21. It is a function, but \(f(-1)=f(1)=0\), so it is not one-to-one.

questions.prompt: Find \(f^{-1}\) for the function \(f(x)=\frac{1}{x+1}\).
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 22. \(y=\frac{1}{x+1}\Rightarrow x+1=\frac1y\Rightarrow x=\frac{1-y}{y}\).

questions.prompt: Find the range of \(f(x)=\frac{1}{x+1}\). [Hint: use the inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)=\frac{1-x}{x}\).]
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 23. The range of \(f\) is the domain of \(f^{-1}(x)=\frac{1-x}{x}\), which is \(x\ne0\).

questions.prompt: For the right triangle shown in the figure, find \(\csc\theta\).
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 24. The hypotenuse is \(\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5\) and the side opposite \(\theta\) is 3, so \(\csc\theta=\frac{\text{hyp}}{\text{opp}}=\frac{5}{3}\).

image.alt: Right triangle with vertical leg 3 and horizontal leg 4; the angle theta is at the end of the leg of length 4, opposite the leg of length 3.

questions.prompt: If \(\tan\theta=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\), then \(\cot\theta=\) ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 25. \(\cot\theta=\frac{1}{\tan\theta}=\sqrt3\).

questions.prompt: Find the reference angle \(\theta'\) for the angle \(\theta=220^\circ\).
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 26. \(220^\circ\) is in the third quadrant: \(\theta'=220^\circ-180^\circ=40^\circ\).

questions.prompt: The exact value of \(\cos\frac{3\pi}{2}\) is ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 27. \(\cos\frac{3\pi}{2}=0\).

questions.prompt: The sine function, \(\sin\), is periodic, and it has period ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 28. \(\sin(x+2\pi)=\sin x\), and \(2\pi\) is the smallest such positive number.

questions.prompt: The range of the cosine function, \(\cos\), is ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 29. \(-1\le\cos x\le 1\), and both values are reached.

questions.prompt: If \(\theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac12\right)\), then \(\cos\theta=\) ...
questions.explanation: Midterm 2024, question 30. \(\theta=\frac{\pi}{6}\), so \(\cos\theta=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\).

questions.prompt: Let \(g(x)=\frac{x-4}{\sqrt{x}-2}\). Then:
questions.explanation: Final 2024, question 1. \(x-4=(\sqrt x-2)(\sqrt x+2)\), so \(g(x)=\sqrt x+2\to4\).

questions.prompt: The value of \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin(x)}{x^3}\) is:
questions.explanation: Final 2024, question 2. \(\frac{\sin x}{x^3}=\frac{\sin x}{x}\cdot\frac{1}{x^2}\) and \(\frac{\sin x}{x}\to1\), \(\frac{1}{x^2}\to+\infty\).

questions.prompt: Let \(\lim_{x\to-\infty}\frac{\cos(5x-3)}{-x^2+x}\). Its value is:
questions.explanation: Final 2024, question 3. \(|\cos(5x-3)|\le1\) while \(|-x^2+x|\to\infty\); by the Sandwich theorem the limit is 0.

questions.prompt: Let \(f(x)=\frac{\sqrt{9x^2-5}}{4x+3}\). Then:
questions.explanation: Final 2024, question 4. For \(x<0\), \(\sqrt{9x^2-5}=|x|\sqrt{9-\frac{5}{x^2}}=-x\sqrt{9-\frac{5}{x^2}}\), so \(f(x)\to\frac{-3}{4}\).

questions.prompt: The limit of \(\frac{x-1}{x^3-1}\) when \(x\) tends to 1 is:
questions.explanation: Final 2024, question 5. \(x^3-1=(x-1)(x^2+x+1)\), so the limit is \(\frac{1}{1+1+1}=\frac13\).

questions.prompt: Let \(f(x)=\frac{-2x+1}{x^2+2x-3}\). Which of the following assertions is true?
options: No one of the previous choices
questions.explanation: Final 2024, question 6. \(x^2+2x-3=(x+3)(x-1)\). As \(x\to-3^+\): numerator \(\to7\), \(x+3\to0^+\), \(x-1\to-4\), so the denominator \(\to0^-\) and \(f\to-\infty\).

questions.prompt: The type of the discontinuity of \(f(x)=\frac{\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)}{x-\frac{\pi}{2}}\) at \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) is:
questions.explanation: Final 2024, question 7. \(f\) is undefined at \(\frac\pi2\) but \(\lim_{x\to\pi/2}f(x)=1\) exists, so the discontinuity is removable.

questions.prompt: Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}\frac{x^2-x-12}{3x^2+6}, & x\ne0\\ A, & x=0\end{cases}\) be a continuous function. Then \(A\) is:
questions.explanation: Final 2024, question 8. Continuity at 0: \(A=\lim_{x\to0}\frac{x^2-x-12}{3x^2+6}=\frac{-12}{6}=-2\).

questions.prompt: Which one fails to satisfy the conditions required for the Intermediate Value Theorem on \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)?
questions.explanation: Final 2024, question 15. The theorem needs \(f\) continuous on the closed interval; \(\tan\) is not even defined at \(\pm\frac{\pi}{2}\).
